summary: The bounded measurement at a98c01f is internally consistent and correctly scoped. measure.py verifies raw layout (32,512,1024) little-endian uint16, checks five reference groups covering panels 0..31 exactly once, requires each group's SHA256 to match the earlier reviewed gate-result.json, and enforces lossless round trips for both codecs before counting bytes (plain LZ4 per 8 KiB block via decompress-equality; bitshuffle via dtype/shape/np.array_equal on the full group). Framing is accounted symmetrically: plain LZ4 uses store_size=False plus 4 bytes per block, bitshuffle's native output already carries 4-byte block lengths; all group sizes are exact multiples of 8192 so no partial-block asymmetry arises. result.json per-stream panels and raw hashes match gate-result.json for all five streams and the same timestamp/event 0. Sums and ratios recomputed by hand match: raw 33,554,432; LZ4 33,710,037 (0.99538x); bitshuffle+LZ4 27,940,162 (1.20094x, 16.7% savings); SLEEK same-event 14,013,832 gives 2.394x and matches the prior codec README. README and scope.md state the limitations required: CPU only, one event, no nvCOMP equivalence, no throughput, not run-wide, lossy-vs-lossless comparison qualified. No findings.
